newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Zalakeramia insists on investment plans.
newsitem.headline: Zalakeramia insists on investment plans.

text.p: Hungarian tile manufacturer Zalakeramia Rt confirmed on Wednesday that it plans to expand abroad, but no projects have been finalised.
"The decision is not ours," Zalakeramia Chairman John T. Rourke told reporters on Wednesday.
"It's the vendor or the politicians of the other country or a whole lot of other people (who decide)," he said.
Company officials declined to be more precise on the acquisition plans they were considering, but earlier they had said the direction was central Europe.
Zalakeramia board members talked to journalists and analysts at the official opening of the recently refurbished Romhany plant that Zalakeramia had acquired last year.
Zalakeramia, Hungary's leading tile maker with a 60 percent stake in domestic production last year, spent 800 million forints for investments in the Romhany plant, keeping the cost in budget.
The plant which has been operating at full capacity since mid-June, will boost Zalakeramia's total output by an annual 1.62 million square metres to around 5.1 million square metres.
While the direction and time of any foreign transaction was undecided Zalakeramia strived for further domestic expansion.
The company will prepare a feasibility study whether the next phase of development should be implemented in Romhany or in the other plant at Tofej, west Hungary, General Director Gyorgy Katona said.
Company officials declined to forecast the 1996 financials apart from that they said they expected to almost double the operating profit from 1995.

In 1995 Zalakeramia posted an operating profit of 772.5 million forints according to International Accounting Standards and 380.0 million according to Hungarian Accounting Standards. Company officials did not say to which figure they referred to.
On the Budapest Stock Exchange Zalakeramia shares closed at 6,950 forints, down 10.
